cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic describes the fused four-view patient geometry for the eight candidate sets. All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. The nearest-pair affinities show that several candidate pairs have between-set affinity close to the within-set range, so the boundaries between those pairs are relatively weak in the fused geometry. Because this tool reports partition-level screening and pair affinities rather than GRV or native-distance label alignment, it does not by itself establish whether the four views share the same candidate boundaries; it characterizes internal structure and boundary proximity in the fused geometry only. Weak pair separation is a review entry point and does not imply that any pair should be merged, and the absence of a dominant internal subdivision signal does not imply that any set should be split.

The exploratory non-driver genes with nominal enrichment all rest on 2/15 versus 0/88 and do not survive global correction. Overall, the mutation evidence for K8_C0002 is a single robust depletion (VHL) plus a weaker, panel-level TP53 enrichment, with no broad coordinated mutation signature across the panel.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic describes the fused four-view patient geometry for the eight candidate sets. All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. The spectral screening is uniform: every set has screen_candidate_k=1, and in each set the leading eigengap (about 0.06 to 0.16) is much larger than all subsequent gaps (about 0.0002 to 0.0027). This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. The nearest-pair affinities show that several candidate pairs have between-set affinity close to the within-set range, so the boundaries between those pairs are relatively weak in the fused geometry. Because this tool reports partition-level screening and pair affinities rather than GRV or native-distance label alignment, it does not by itself establish whether the four views share the same candidate boundaries; it characterizes internal structure and boundary proximity in the fused geometry only. Weak pair separation is a review entry point and does not imply that any pair should be merged, and the absence of a dominant internal subdivision signal does not imply that any set should be split.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic describes the fused four-view patient geometry for the eight candidate sets. All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. The spectral screening is uniform: every set has screen_candidate_k=1, and in each set the leading eigengap (about 0.06 to 0.16) is much larger than all subsequent gaps (about 0.0002 to 0.0027). This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. The nearest-pair affinities show that several candidate pairs have between-set affinity close to the within-set range, so the boundaries between those pairs are relatively weak in the fused geometry. Because this tool reports partition-level screening and pair affinities rather than GRV or native-distance label alignment, it does not by itself establish whether the four views share the same candidate boundaries; it characterizes internal structure and boundary proximity in the fused geometry only. Weak pair separation is a review entry point and does not imply that any pair should be merged, and the absence of a dominant internal subdivision signal does not imply that any set should be split.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with the partition geometry, but the magnitudes and the separation of location from dispersion effects vary. In the fused geometry, tissue source site has a significant PERMANOVA location association (q 0.0025) with a small R-squared (0.0497) and no detectable PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.434), indicating a modest location shift without dispersion confounding. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase has the largest location association (R-squared 0.154, q 0.0025) but also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.0285), so its PERMANOVA result may partly reflect dispersion; the large UNKNOWN level (40/103) also limits interpretability. CT slice thickness and CT z-spacing show the strongest distance-regression associations (R-squared 0.136 and 0.142, both q 0.002), indicating that acquisition geometry is associated with CT distances. CT manufacturer has a significant location association (q 0.0067) with a significant dispersion difference (q 0.009), so its location result may partly reflect dispersion, and the Philips level has only 3 observations. CT pixel spacing and study year are significant but with small R-squared values (0.019 and 0.029). CT reconstruction kernel and CT scanner model are only nominally associated (p 0.048 and 0.054) and do not survive correction; their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because of sparse levels. These are association measures, not proof of technical artifact or causation, and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding. The pattern indicates that site and CT acquisition factors are associated with the geometry and warrant consideration, but the small R-squared values for most factors mean they do not by themselves account for a large share of the geometry.
